summary: The candidate captures most of the paper's central degree-theoretic chain, including degree and winding number, the degree-zero criterion, the extension theorem, the Hopf degree theorem, the Poincare-Hopf application, and the computation of pi_k(S^k). It is nevertheless weakened by several substantive mathematical errors, missing hypotheses, inconsistent classifications and locators, and substantial duplication. The most serious defects are the false torus Euler-characteristic formula, reversed sphere-homotopy inequalities, an incorrectly quantified epsilon-neighborhood theorem, and omission of the isolated-zero definition and hypotheses needed for the vector-field results.
strengths: Extracts the main Hopf degree theorem and correctly represents equality of degree as the homotopy criterion.
Captures the principal supporting chain involving local degree, signed preimage counts, degree-zero null-homotopy, punctured Euclidean space, extension, and range adjustment.
Includes the conclusion pi_k(S^k) is isomorphic to Z and connects it to degree.
Covers the vector-field application through finite-zero constructions, zero removal, Poincare-Hopf, the Euler-characteristic criterion, and the hairy-ball consequence.
Marks several imported background results as external, including isotopy, linear isotopy, Sard, transversality extension, the epsilon-neighborhood theorem, and Poincare-Hopf.
Most displayed formulas have balanced LaTeX delimiters and most page locators lie near the corresponding source material.
issues: The entry for sphere and torus Euler characteristics falsely states chi(T^k) = -2(k-2); the verified value is chi(T^k) = 0.
The claimed vanishing pi_k(S^n) = 0 for n < k is false, and it is immediately contradicted by the correctly cited nontrivial class in pi_3(S^2). The stable dimensional inequality was reversed.
The Hopf-fibration entry likewise says nontrivial classes occur when k < n even though its example pi_3(S^2) has k > n.

The epsilon-neighborhood theorem incorrectly quantifies over arbitrary epsilon and inadequately states the nearest-point projection result; only a sufficiently small tubular neighborhood is guaranteed.

The Poincare-Hopf entry omits the finite isolated-zero condition and the no-boundary hypothesis, while the nonvanishing-vector-field theorem also omits the no-boundary hypothesis. As written, these statements are overbroad.
The definition of the index of an isolated vector-field zero, foundational for the vector-field section, is absent.
The finite-zero vector-field entry only asserts existence of some such field, missing the stronger perturbation statement represented in the Gold artifact.
The hairy-ball entry covers only S^2 rather than all even-dimensional spheres S^{2m}; the odd-dimensional existence statement is also omitted.
Sard's theorem is classified as a lemma and reduced to a description of how it is used, rather than extracting its mathematical statement about critical values.
The transversality homotopy theorem is missing, and the extracted transversality extension theorem is too vague to preserve its domain, target, submanifold, and relative-boundary conditions.
The stereographic-projection entry is vague, describes the spaces imprecisely, and is located on page 5 rather than the Gold locator on page 13.

There is excessive duplication: boundary extension, degree-zero sphere null-homotopy, punctured-space null-homotopy, range adjustment, and finite-zero vector-field claims recur under multiple IDs. One ID, hopf:claim:finite-zero-vector-field, is reused for two different statements.
Many supporting lemmas are classified as theorems, reducing entry-type fidelity even when their underlying content is usable.

entryLevelComparison.notes: Faithful definition with useful signed-intersection detail.
Missing the sufficiently-small-epsilon condition and misstating the projection conclusion.
Contains the Gold self-map theorem as a special case of the stated manifold-to-sphere result.
Correctly states that degree identifies pi_k(S^k) with Z, though the explicit k >= 1 condition is omitted.
No entry defines isolated-zero index as the degree of the normalized boundary-sphere map.
The main equality is present and externally attributed, but necessary boundary and isolated-zero hypotheses are missing.
Sphere values are correct, but the torus formula is false.
The equivalence is captured but the no-boundary condition is omitted.
Only the classical S^2 instance is extracted, not the full even-dimensional statement.
The general perturbation-to-transversality theorem used in the finite-zero argument is not represented.
